symptoms: Center diff orange light blinks after driving 10 min in 2H
diagnosticSteps: 1. Scan 4WD ECU (identifies exact switch: 2WD/4WD, Center Diff Lock, or High/Low switch on transfer case!). 2. Check vacuum solenoid valves on right fender apron. 3. Replace faulty plunger switch.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: 4WD Front Axle Won't Engage (ADD / Vacuum Hub Fault)
phContext: Toyota Hilux/Fortuner (ADD motor), Mitsubishi (freewheel clutch)
symptoms: 4H light blinks, front driveshaft spins but front wheels don't pull
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect front differential ADD actuator (Toyota) or vacuum hoses & solenoid (Mitsubishi). 2. Check ADD motor limit switch contacts for gear oil seepage. 3. Clean & reseal.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Driveline Binding / Hopping on Dry Pavement — Stuck in 4H/Lock
phContext: Driver accidentally engaged 4H Part-Time or Rear Diff Lock on dry asphalt
symptoms: Vehicle hops/scrubs tires during tight U-turns, heavy steering
diagnosticSteps: 1. Verify 4WD selector is in 2H and Rear Diff Lock button is OFF! 2. Reverse 5–10 meters in a straight line to relieve driveline wind-up torque so actuator can disengage. 3. Inspect actuator.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Rear Differential Lock Position Switch Fault — Mud/Water
phContext: Toyota Hilux/Fortuner, Ford Ranger, Isuzu; submerged rear axle plug
symptoms: Diff Lock light blinks endlessly, rear locker stuck or disabled
diagnosticSteps: 1. Unplug 2-pin/5-pin connector on rear differential housing and inspect for mud/broken wire. 2. Test diff-lock motor 12V/ground and limit switch continuity. 3. Clean & seal.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Transfer Case Differential Lock-Up Solenoid (Ford/Mazda)
phContext: Ford Ranger/Everest 4x4; broken wire above transfer case
symptoms: 4WD wrench light on, 4WD disabled
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect transfer case shift motor 7-pin/2-pin harness for driveshaft rub or mud damage. 2. Measure coil resistance (5–15 ohms). 3. Repair wire.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: AWD Coupling Overheating Warning on Steep Dirt Climb
phContext: Subaru Forester, Honda CR-V, Hyundai Tucson, Kia Sorento AWD
symptoms: 'AWD Temp High — 2WD Mode Active' on steep muddy climb
diagnosticSteps: 1. Stop and let rear electro-hydraulic/magnetic AWD coupling cool 15 min. 2. Inspect rear diff/coupling fluid (often dark/burnt at 60,000 km!). 3. Check mismatched tire tread depths (kills AWD!).

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Suspension / Ride Height Sensor Circuit — Snapped Plastic Arm
phContext: SUVs with adaptive dampers or air suspension; pothole/off-road snap
symptoms: Suspension warning light, harsh/stiff ride
diagnosticSteps: 1. Visually inspect all corner ride-height sensors inside wheel wells for snapped plastic linkage arms. 2. Check 5V, GND, and signal sweep (0.5–4.5V). 3. Replace link & calibrate height.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Air Suspension Sagging Overnight (One Corner) — Leaky Air Spring
phContext: Luxury SUVs/vans (Lexus, Land Cruiser, Mercedes, BMW) in PH heat
symptoms: Rear or front corner sitting on bump stops every morning
diagnosticSteps: 1. Spray soapy water on rubber air-spring bellows fold and brass airline fitting while inflated. 2. Listen for hiss when parked. 3. Replace cracked air spring before compressor burns out.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Air Suspension Compressor Overheating / Slow Fill — Worn Ring
phContext: SUVs running with leaky air bag burning out compressor
symptoms: Compressor runs 2+ min at every start, then shuts down with fault
diagnosticSteps: 1. Fix air spring leak FIRST! 2. Measure compressor current draw and output pressure (must reach >10 bar quickly). 3. Rebuild compressor piston ring & silica drier.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Clunking Noise Over Speed Bumps — Worn Stabilizer Link / Bushings
phContext: All PH sedans/MPVs/SUVs (Vios, Xpander, City, Hilux) on lubak
symptoms: Hollow knocking sound over small bumps at 10–30 km/h
diagnosticSteps: 1. Grab sway bar end-links and rock firmly (or pry sway bar bushings) with car on ground! 2. Replace torn stabilizer links & rubber D-bushings.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Creaking / Squeaking When Turning — Dry Lower Ball Joint
phContext: Pickups/SUVs (Hilux, Montero, Navara, Innova); torn rubber boot
symptoms: Loud rubber/metal groan when turning steering wheel parked
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect lower ball joint rubber boot for tears letting floodwater in (dangerous — worn ball joint can snap!). 2. Check vertical play with prybar under tire. 3. Replace ball joint immediately.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Rear Leaf Spring Squeak / Sag — Broken Overload Leaf
phContext: Commercial pickups & vans (Hilux, L300, HiAce, Traviz) overloaded
symptoms: Loud squeak over bumps, rear sits uneven left-to-right
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect leaf spring stack for cracked leaf or missing nylon anti-friction pads between leaves. 2. Check U-bolt torque and shackle bushings. 3. Replace worn bushings/leaf.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: 4x4 Manual Locking Hub Stuck — Dried Grease / Rust
phContext: Older 4x4 pickups/SUVs with AVM/Aisin manual freewheeling hubs
symptoms: Hub dial won't turn from FREE to LOCK
diagnosticSteps: 1. Remove 6 Allen bolts on hub dial (in FREE position), clean old hardened grease and rust. 2. Lightly coat splines with thin marine grease (thick grease prevents spring engagement!). 3. Reassemble.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Humming / Vibration Only in 4H Above 40 km/h — Front Driveshaft
phContext: Lifted 4x4 pickups; worn front double-cardan U-joint
symptoms: Buzzing vibration in floorboard in 4H, completely gone in 2H
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check front driveshaft U-joints and centering ball for play. 2. Check driveshaft phase and slip-yoke spline wear. 3. Balance/rebuild front driveshaft.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: AWD Transfer / Coupling Solenoid Circuit Open — Underbody Wire
phContext: Hyundai/Kia/Honda/Nissan AWD; torn wire near rear differential
symptoms: AWD warning light solid, front-wheel drive only
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect 2-pin connector on rear differential electromagnetic coupling for road-debris tear. 2. Measure coil resistance (typically 2–5 ohms). 3. Repair wire.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Car Wanders / Unstable at 100 km/h — Torn Lower Control Arm Bushing
phContext: High-mileage Vios, Mirage, City, Innova; cracked compliance bushing
symptoms: Steering feels vague on expressway, clunks when braking
diagnosticSteps: 1. Look at large vertical rubber bushing at rear of front lower control arm for deep cracks/tears. 2. Pry with bar to check excessive deflection. 3. Replace bushings/arms + align.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: CV Axle Clicking Loudly on Tight U-Turns — Torn Outer Boot
phContext: FWD sedans/MPVs (Vios, Xpander, City, Mirage); grit in outer CV joint
symptoms: Rhythmic 'tok-tok-tok' only when turning full lock under gas
diagnosticSteps: 1. Turn wheel full lock and inspect outer CV rubber boot for grease sling/tear. 2. Replace outer CV joint or complete axle shaft. 3. Check inner tripod boot too.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Whole Car Shakes Under Acceleration (40–70 km/h), Stops Coasting
phContext: FWD cars & lifted pickups; worn inner CV tripod joint
symptoms: Side-to-side wobble only when pressing gas, smooth when coasting
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect inner CV axle cup for radial play (unlike outer CV, worn inner CV shakes straight ahead under torque!). 2. Replace worn inner CV axle.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Shock Absorber Oil Leak & Bouncing — Blown Strut Seal
phContext: Cars hitting deep potholes; oil-soaked strut body
symptoms: Car bounces 3+ times after speed bump, nose dives hard braking
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect shock absorber body for wet oil + dust cake. 2. Check tire tread for cupping/scalloping wear. 3. Replace shocks/struts in pairs + upper strut mounts.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Front Strut Mount Knock When Turning — Seized Bearing
phContext: McPherson strut cars (Vios, Mirage, City, Xpander); rusted top bearing
symptoms: Metallic 'boing/twang' from coil spring when turning wheel
diagnosticSteps: 1. Hold coil spring while assistant turns steering wheel (you will feel spring bind and snap!). 2. Replace top strut bearing/mount in pairs.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: 4WD System Disabled by ABS Wheel Speed Fault
phContext: Toyota/Ford/Mitsubishi 4x4; any wheel speed sensor fault locks out 4WD
symptoms: 4WD light flashing + ABS light on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Scan ABS module first (4WD ECU relies on all 4 wheel speeds to prevent diff bind!). 2. Fix faulty wheel speed sensor. 3. Clear both ABS and 4WD codes.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Rear Differential Whining on Throttle Only (60–90 km/h)
phContext: High-mileage pickups/vans/jeepneys; worn ring & pinion gear
symptoms: Howling noise when pressing gas, quiet when coasting
diagnosticSteps: 1. Drain diff oil to inspect for metallic paste/chips (check if water entered breather!). 2. Check pinion nut torque/bearing play. 3. Rebuild diff gear backlash/bearings.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Engine/Transmission Mount Vibration at Stoplight in Drive
phContext: Honda City/Civic, Toyota Vios/Camry, Mitsubishi; collapsed hydraulic mount
symptoms: Dashboard & steering wheel vibrate heavily at idle in D, smooth in N
diagnosticSteps: 1. Watch engine movement while power-braking gently in D and R (excessive rock = torn mount). 2. Inspect right-side hydraulic engine mount for oil leak/collapsed gap. 3. Replace OEM mount.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Tire Pulling Hard Left/Right — Radial Ply Belt Separation
phContext: Tires hit pothole or aged >5 years in PH heat
symptoms: Car pulls strongly to one side even after alignment, wobble at low speed
diagnosticSteps: 1. Swap front left and front right tires! If pull reverses to the opposite side, the tire has radial belt separation (not alignment!). 2. Inspect inner sidewall for bulge (bukol). 3. Replace tire.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Adaptive Damper / Magnetic Ride Solenoid Open — Wheel Well
phContext: Performance/luxury SUVs; broken damper wire at strut top/bottom
symptoms: Suspension fault on cluster, ride locked firm
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect 2-pin connector on top/bottom of shock absorber. 2. Measure damper solenoid coil (typically 2–5 ohms). 3. Repair wire.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: 4x4 Front Differential Carrier Bushing Clunk — Shift to D/R
phContext: IFS pickups/SUVs; torn front diff mounting bushings
symptoms: Heavy clunk under front floor when shifting Drive to Reverse
diagnosticSteps: 1. Watch front differential housing move while shifting D <-> R with brake held. 2. Replace torn rubber diff support bushings. 3. Check driveshaft U-joints.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Steering Shimmy Braking at 100 km/h + Loose Thrust Arm
phContext: SUVs/sedans; worn control arm bushing amplifying slight rotor runout
symptoms: Steering wheel oscillates violently on highway braking
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect front lower control arm rear bushings AND measure rotor runout. 2. Fixing only rotors returns vibration in 3,000 km if bushings are torn! 3. Replace both.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Rear Torsion Beam Axle Bushings Torn — Rear Steer Feel
phContext: Vios, Mirage, City, Xpander; cracked rear axle pivot bushings
symptoms: Rear end feels loose/steps out over expansion joints on Skyway
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect large rubber pivot bushings where rear torsion beam bolts to body. 2. Replace torn rear axle bushings. 3. Check rear alignment.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Transfer Case Shift Fork Position Switch Mismatch
phContext: Ford/Toyota/Nissan 4x4; corroded encoder ring inside shift motor
symptoms: 4WD stuck between 4H and 4L (neutral!), car won't move
diagnosticSteps: 1. Remove 4WD shift motor, manually index transfer case shaft back to 2H so vehicle can drive. 2. Open motor encoder plate and clean oxidized contact tracks. 3. Replace motor.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Overloaded Pickup Rear Bottoming Out — Worn Bump Stops
phContext: Delivery pickups/vans carrying heavy cargo daily
symptoms: Harsh slam over dips, tail lights aimed at sky
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect missing/crushed rubber bump stops and weak leaf springs/coils. 2. Install helper springs or upgraded heavy-duty shocks. 3. Aim headlights properly.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Wheel Lug Studs Stripped / Loose — Over-Torqued by Impact Gun
phContext: Cars serviced at roadside vulcanizing shops using uncalibrated air guns
symptoms: Vibration, squeaking wheel, snapped wheel studs
diagnosticSteps: 1. Always torque lug nuts with calibrated torque wrench (typically 100–120 N·m cars, 130–150 N·m pickups). 2. Replace stretched/stripped studs. 3. Never use oil/grease on dry lug threads.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Subframe Creak / Pop on Steep Driveway — Loose Subframe Bolts
phContext: Cars after clutch/steering rack job; under-torqued cradle bolts
symptoms: Single loud metallic 'pop' when turning into steep ramp
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check torque on all front engine cradle / subframe mounting bolts. 2. Inspect for missing alignment sleeves. 3. Torque to OEM spec.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Electronic Rear Diff / e-LSD Fault — Overheated Clutch Pack
phContext: Performance/AWD SUVs; spinning one wheel in deep mud
symptoms: 'AWD/Diff Lock Overheated' warning
diagnosticSteps: 1. Stop and cool diff 15 min. 2. Change rear diff/e-LSD fluid immediately if cooked. 3. Check e-LSD pump/actuator motor.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Panhard Rod / Track Bar Bushings Worn — 'Death Wobble'
phContext: Solid-front-axle 4x4s (Jimny, Wrangler, older Land Cruiser)
symptoms: Violent uncontrollable steering shake after hitting bump at 60+ km/h
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect track bar (Panhard rod) frame & axle bushings for any play while assistant rocks steering wheel! 2. Check kingpin bearings, tie rods, and steering damper. 3. Replace worn bushings.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Exhaust Hanger Broken — Metallic Rattle Against Rear Axle
phContext: Low cars hitting speed bumps; torn rubber exhaust hanger
symptoms: Loud buzzing/clanging under rear seat at idle or bumps
diagnosticSteps: 1. Shake tailpipe cold to locate contact against heat shield or rear axle. 2. Replace torn rubber exhaust hangers and bend heat shield clear. 3. Check catalytic converter heat shield clamps.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Spare Tire Carrier Cable Rusted Seized — Flat Tire Emergency
phContext: Pickups/MPVs (Hilux, Ranger, Innova, Xpander) with underbody winch
symptoms: Winch cable jams or snaps when lowering spare tire
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect and lubricate underbody spare tire winch mechanism every 6 months! 2. Replace rusted winch assembly before emergency. 3. Check spare tire PSI.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: 4WD / Hill Descent Control Fault — Brake Temp Too High
phContext: SUVs descending long mountain roads with HDC active continuously
symptoms: HDC light flashes and disables
diagnosticSteps: 1. Allow brakes to cool (ECU estimates rotor temp >350°C and disables HDC!). 2. Use low gear (L/M1/M2) engine braking instead of riding brakes. 3. Verify no brake switch fault.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Front Hub Freewheel Bearing / Needle Bearing Growl
phContext: 4x4 pickups (Hilux, Ranger, Tacoma) in 2H mode
symptoms: Low growling/vibration at 50–70 km/h that vanishes when switched to 4H!
diagnosticSteps: 1. Test drive at 60 km/h and switch to 4H briefly: if noise vanishes instantly, front diff CV axle needle bearing is worn! 2. Replace front diff carrier needle bearing.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Torsion Bar Sagging (Older Pickups/SUVs) — Uneven Ride Height
phContext: Older Mitsubishi Adventure/Strada, Isuzu Crosswind/D-Max, Hilux
symptoms: Front end hits bump stops constantly, negative camber eating inner tires
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure fender-to-hub height left vs. right. 2. Adjust torsion bar anchor bolts evenly (replace fatigued torsion bars if maxed out). 3. Re-align front wheels.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Aftermarket Wheel Spacers Causing Vibration — Non-Hubcentric
phContext: Modified pickups/SUVs; lug-centric cheap spacers
symptoms: Steering shake above 80 km/h
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check if wheel spacer lacks hub-centric lip matching vehicle hub bore (e.g., 106.1mm Toyota, 93.1mm Ford). 2. Remove or use precision billet hub-centric spacers only. 3. Check lug thread engagement.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Sway Bar Link Snapped — Body Roll & Clunk
phContext: SUVs/crossovers hitting deep roadside culvert
symptoms: Scary body lean in corners, metallic clatter
diagnosticSteps: 1. Visually inspect both ends of front/rear anti-roll bar. 2. Replace snapped end-links in pairs. 3. Check ABS wire clipped to strut (often torn when link snaps!).

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Brake Caliper Mounting Bracket Bolt Loose — Clunk on Reverse
phContext: Vehicles after recent brake pad/rotor job; un-torqued bracket bolt
symptoms: Sharp metallic clank first time braking in Reverse, then again in Drive
diagnosticSteps: 1. Immediately inspect caliper bracket bolts! (Lost bolt lets caliper flip into rim!). 2. Apply blue threadlocker and torque to spec.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: 4WD Mode Switch Signal Error — Spilled Drink in Console
phContext: Console-mounted 4WD rotary dial (Ranger, Fortuner, Montero)
symptoms: 4WD doesn't respond to dial turns, C1299 stored
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read 4WD Switch Position PIDs while turning dial (2H/4H/4L). 2. Remove dial and clean sticky coffee/soda off PCB contacts. 3. Replace switch if resistor ladder damaged.

domainName: Electronic Suspension, AWD/4WD Couplings, Diff Locks & Chassis
title: Pitman / Idler Arm Play — Wandering Steering (Older SUVs)
phContext: Older Pajero, Crosswind, L300, Frontier; worn steering box linkages
symptoms: 2+ inches of dead play at steering wheel center
diagnosticSteps: 1. Have assistant rock steering wheel while inspecting Pitman arm, Idler arm, and center drag link for vertical/lateral play. 2. Replace worn idler arm bushings & grease.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Auto Start-Stop (i-Stop / ISS) Disabled — Standard Battery Installed
phContext: Mazda, Ford, Nissan, Suzuki SHVS; shop replaced EFB/AGM with cheap wet battery
symptoms: ISS / i-Stop light flashes amber, engine never shuts off at stops
diagnosticSteps: 1. Verify battery type: Start-Stop systems require EFB or AGM battery (standard flooded battery fails internal resistance check!). 2. Install EFB/AGM and perform BMS / i-Stop initialization.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Suzuki SHVS Mild Hybrid ISG Fault — Weak Belt / Sub-Battery
phContext: Suzuki Ertiga Hybrid, XL7 Hybrid; 12V Lithium-Ion under-seat battery
symptoms: ISG warning light, Engine Auto Stop-Start disabled
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check SHVS tensioner and specialized rib belt (ISG cranks engine via belt!). 2. Scan ISG module for 12V Li-ion sub-battery SOC/temp faults (under front passenger seat). 3. Check 12V lead-acid health.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Smart Alternator Drops to 12.6V While Driving — Normal vs. Fault
phContext: Ford, Mazda, Hyundai, Honda ELD; regenerative/load-shedding charging
symptoms: Driver panics seeing 12.5V on aftermarket voltmeter while cruising
diagnosticSteps: 1. Explain smart charging: ECM drops alternator to ~12.6V when battery is >80% SOC, then boosts to 14.5V on decel or headlights ON! 2. Turn headlights ON; if voltage jumps to 14.2V, system is healthy.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Honda ELD (Electronic Load Detector) Fault — Low Idle Voltage
phContext: Honda City, Jazz, Civic, CR-V; failed ELD module inside fuse box
symptoms: Voltage drops to 12.2V at idle with headlights OFF, battery dies slowly
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read ELD Load Current PID in Honda ECM (stuck at 0A or max). 2. Turn headlights ON; if voltage jumps to 14.3V, alternator is good and ELD in engine fuse box is faulty. 3. Replace ELD.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Lost Comm with Active Grille Shutter — Bumper Hit / Mud
phContext: Ford Focus/EcoSport/Territory, Honda, modern crossovers
symptoms: MIL on, battery/charging or cooling fan erratic (shares LIN bus!)
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect Active Grille Shutter behind front bumper for jammed plastic vanes or unplugged LIN connector. 2. NOTE: On Ford, a shorted grille shutter often pulls down the LIN bus shared with the alternator! 3. Unplug to test.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Battery Monitoring Sensor (BMS) Broken Wire at Negative Post
phContext: Ford, Hyundai, Kia, Mazda, BYD; thin 2-pin plug on negative clamp
symptoms: Battery warning light, Start-Stop disabled, fixed 13.8V charging
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect tiny 2-pin connector on negative battery terminal (often snapped when mechanics yank battery out!). 2. Repair broken LIN/power wire. 3. Reset BMS.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Engine Fails to Restart After Auto Start-Stop at Traffic Light
phContext: Aging Start-Stop vehicles with weak starter or sulfated EFB battery
symptoms: Engine shuts off at red light, then stalls/won't crank on green!
diagnosticSteps: 1. Load-test EFB/AGM battery immediately (cranking voltage <9.0V drops out ECM during hot restart!). 2. Check starter motor cycle counter (some OEMs lock out ISS at max cycles). 3. Replace battery/starter.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Suzuki SHVS Under-Seat Lithium Sub-Battery Flooded
phContext: Suzuki Ertiga/XL7 Hybrid driven in cabin-deep floodwater
symptoms: SHVS warning on dash, parasitic drain or no regenerative assist
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect 12V Li-ion auxiliary battery pack under front passenger seat for water line/corrosion. 2. Scan ISG/Li-ion BMS for cell imbalance or isolation error. 3. Dry/replace pack.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Mazda i-Stop Blinking Amber After Battery Disconnect
phContext: Mazda 2, 3, CX-5; battery disconnected without i-Stop relearn
symptoms: Amber 'i-stop' light blinks continuously
diagnosticSteps: 1. Verify battery SOC >75% and engine fully warm. 2. Perform Mazda i-Stop Battery Current Sensor Initialization + Steering Angle reset via scan tool or pedal/switch sequence. 3. Clear DTCs.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Jump-Start Pack / Booster Connected to Negative Post Damages BMS
phContext: Drivers clamping jumper negative directly to battery (-) post bypassing BMS
symptoms: BMS SOC reads wrong (thinks battery is still dead), Start-Stop off
diagnosticSteps: 1. Always clamp jumper negative to bare engine/chassis ground stud (NOT battery negative post!) so BMS shunt measures charge current. 2. Reset BMS or let car sleep 8 hours locked.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Generator Field/F Terminal Circuit Low — Shorted Rotor/Wire
phContext: Hyundai, Kia, Ford, Honda; shorted alternator field
symptoms: Battery light on, no charging (12.0V), blown ALT fuse
diagnosticSteps: 1. Unplug alternator control plug and test field wire for short to ground. 2. Measure rotor slip-ring resistance (2–5 ohms; <1 ohm = shorted rotor). 3. Replace alternator.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Generator Field/F Terminal Circuit High — Short to 12V / Open
phContext: Alternator field wire shorted to battery positive
symptoms: Overcharging (>15.5V) or battery light on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Unplug alternator and check harness field pin (should not have full 12V key-on unless ECM commands). 2. Replace faulty voltage regulator.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Alternator Pulley Nut Backed Off — No Charging & Squeal
phContext: Rebuilt alternators where pulley nut wasn't impact-tightened
symptoms: Sudden battery light, pulley spinning freely on shaft
diagnosticSteps: 1. Remove belt and check if alternator pulley nut is loose/spinning on shaft! 2. Inspect shaft threads and OAP splines. 3. Torque new OAP pulley properly.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Starter Heat Soak Next to Exhaust Manifold — No Crank Hot
phContext: V6/turbo/headers where starter sits inches from hot exhaust
symptoms: Cranks strong cold, dead click after highway run; starts after 30 min
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure 12V at starter S-terminal during hot no-crank (if 12V is solid, solenoid coil is heat-soaking open!). 2. Check missing starter heat shield. 3. Replace starter & add heat shield.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: High-Current Mega-Fuse (200A–300A) Hairline Crack
phContext: Ford, Hyundai, European cars; hairline thermal crack in battery-box fuse
symptoms: Intermittent total power loss or alternator no-charge until tapped
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure voltage on BOTH sides of high-current bolt-on mega-fuses while wiggling fuse body! 2. Look for hairline crack in fuse element window. 3. Replace mega-fuse.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Control Module Vehicle Options / Battery Config Error (Ford)
phContext: Ford Ranger/Everest after battery size/type change in BCM
symptoms: Wrench light on, charging erratic
diagnosticSteps: 1. Verify selected battery capacity (Ah) and type (EFB/AGM) in BCM matches installed battery. 2. Run PCM Module Initialization. 3. Clear P160A.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Dual-Battery Isolator / VSR Sticking (Overland Pickups)
phContext: Hilux/Ranger/Montero overland rigs with 2nd auxiliary battery in bed
symptoms: Starter battery drains overnight when fridge/inverter runs
diagnosticSteps: 1. Test Voltage Sensitive Relay (VSR) / DC-DC charger cutoff (must open below ~12.7V). 2. Check if VSR solenoid contacts welded closed. 3. Upgrade to smart DC-DC charger.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Alternator Fan Blade Scraping Housing — Bent After Drop
phContext: Aftermarket/rebuilt alternator dropped during shipping/install
symptoms: Metallic ticking noise from alternator proportional to RPM
diagnosticSteps: 1. Spin alternator by hand with belt off to hear scrape. 2. Inspect external/internal cooling fan fins. 3. Clear bent fin or replace.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Starter Ring Gear Missing Teeth — Grinding at Specific Spot
phContext: High-mileage taxis/vans; engine always stops at 2 compression spots
symptoms: Horrible grinding noise on some cranks, starts fine on others
diagnosticSteps: 1. Remove starter and bar crankshaft over 360° while inspecting flywheel ring gear teeth! 2. Replace flywheel ring gear if teeth are chewed flat. 3. Replace starter pinion.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Battery Terminal Clamp Stretched — Loose Even Tightened Max
phContext: Soft lead-alloy clamps tightened too far over years
symptoms: Bolt bottomed out, clamp still twists by hand on battery post
diagnosticSteps: 1. Never jam screws/nails between clamp and post! 2. Replace stretched battery terminal clamp (or use proper lead post shim temporarily). 3. Clean & torque.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: System Voltage Malfunction — Corroded Positive Distribution Stud
phContext: Cars with remote underhood jump-start post (Ford, BMW, Mazda)
symptoms: Erratic voltage at ECUs despite 12.6V at trunk/under-seat battery
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure voltage drop from battery (+) post to underhood jump-start B+ stud under load. 2. Clean corroded bulkhead pass-through stud! 3. Check 100A+ main fuse.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Aftermarket Voltmeter Reads 11.8V in Cigarette Socket — Drop Only
phContext: Driver alarmed by cheap 12V plug-in voltmeter showing low voltage
symptoms: Voltmeter reads 11.8V with A/C + wipers on, battery tests 14.1V!
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure directly at battery posts with calibrated DMM (14.1V = charging fine!). 2. Explain voltage drop across thin ACC socket wiring + high-draw accessories. 3. Check ground.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: ISG / Belt-Starter Slipping on Wet Morning Startup
phContext: Suzuki SHVS / mild hybrids with glazed belt or weak tensioner
symptoms: Loud belt squeal for 1 sec on Auto-Restart at stoplight
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect specialized heavy-duty SHVS serpentine belt ribs and tensioner damper. 2. Replace belt and tensioner if pulley chirps. 3. Verify no coolant/oil drip on belt.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Push-Start Button Needs 3–4 Presses to Crank — Dirty Contact
phContext: 5+ year old push-button cars (Vios, City, Xpander, Montero)
symptoms: Pressing Start turns ACC/ON, takes multiple tries to crank
diagnosticSteps: 1. Monitor Start-Stop Button 1 & 2 switch PIDs in BCM while pressing lightly vs. firmly. 2. Check brake switch PID simultaneously. 3. Replace worn Start-Stop switch.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Battery Discharging When Parked — Bluetooth / Key Fob Too Close
phContext: Smart-key car parked in garage 2 meters from key hook inside house!
symptoms: Keyless LF antennas stay awake pinging fob all night, battery dies in 3 days
diagnosticSteps: 1. Store smart keys >5 meters away or in Faraday pouch! 2. Measure parasitic draw with key nearby vs. far away to verify. 3. Check door handle request button stuck pressed.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Generator Lamp/L Terminal Circuit — Shorted Cluster/Wire
phContext: Older/mid-2000s vehicles; battery light never lights up at KOEO!
symptoms: Battery dies because alternator never receives excitation current!
diagnosticSteps: 1. Turn key ON engine OFF: verify Battery Warning Lamp lights up! (On many cars, excitation current flows THROUGH that bulb/resistor!). 2. Check L-wire continuity to cluster. 3. Fix lamp/wire.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Alternator Overheating — Missing Air Duct / Splash Shield
phContext: Compact cars with tight engine bays; missing plastic alternator scoop
symptoms: Alternator regulator fails every 6 months in traffic
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check if factory plastic cooling duct or lower splash shield is missing. 2. Restore air ducting and clean oil/mud off alternator cooling vents. 3. Test charging ripple.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: 12V Battery Dead After Car Wash / Detailing — Doors Left Open
phContext: Detailers leaving doors/trunk open 3 hours with interior/welcome lights on
symptoms: Car won't crank at pickup, low-voltage U-codes everywhere
diagnosticSteps: 1. Charge battery fully with smart charger (don't just rely on 10-min alternator idle!). 2. Load-test battery after full charge. 3. Clear all low-voltage U-codes.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Hybrid/ISS Auxiliary Battery Temp Sensor — Unplugged/Missing
phContext: Suzuki SHVS / Mazda / Ford; temp sensor under battery tray
symptoms: Start-Stop disabled, battery temp reads -40°C
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect 2-pin thermistor under battery tray or clipped to battery side. 2. Measure resistance (~10 kΩ at 25°C). 3. Reconnect/replace sensor.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Engine Cranks Slowly in Cold Baguio Morning — Wrong Thick Oil
phContext: Cars running 20W-50 mineral oil in cool highlands
symptoms: Sluggish cranking, slow oil pressure buildup
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check oil viscosity used (20W-50 thickens heavily at 10–15°C!). 2. Switch to OEM-spec 5W-30 / 0W-20 synthetic. 3. Load-test battery.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Remote Start / Alarm Kills Engine After 10 Seconds — Tach Sense
phContext: Aftermarket remote-start alarms without proper tach/voltage sense
symptoms: Remote start cranks, fires, then shuts down after 10 sec
diagnosticSteps: 1. Re-learn remote-start tach signal (or switch from voltage-sense to true injector/CKP tach wire). 2. Check immobilizer bypass module.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Alternator Case Grounded Poorly — Painted Mounting Bracket
phContext: Cars with newly powder-coated or painted alternator bracket
symptoms: Charging voltage fluctuates 12.8– 13.6V, alternator gets hot
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure voltage drop from alternator aluminum housing to battery negative post (<0.15V). 2. Scrape paint off bracket contact ears or add dedicated 8 AWG ground wire. 3. Retest.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Key Stuck in Ignition Cylinder — Dead Battery / Park Switch
phContext: Automatic cars (Ford, Hyundai, Nissan) with electronic key interlock
symptoms: Key turns to ACC, refuses to pull out
diagnosticSteps: 1. Jump-start or charge 12V battery (shift-interlock solenoid needs 12V to release key!). 2. Jiggle shifter firmly into Park (check P indicator on dash). 3. Use manual key-release pinhole if available.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Starter Solenoid Sticks Engaged on Weak Battery — Weld
phContext: Low voltage (<9V) during cranking causes solenoid arc-welding
symptoms: Starter keeps cranking even after key is pulled out!
diagnosticSteps: 1. Disconnect battery negative immediately! 2. Replace welded starter solenoid and load-test/replace weak battery that caused the low-voltage arc. 3. Check starter relay.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: High Voltage Spike (>16V) — Disconnecting Battery While Running
phContext: Old-school mechanic trick: pulling battery cable to 'test alternator'
symptoms: Fried ECM/ABS/Radio immediately after 'testing' alternator!
diagnosticSteps: 1. NEVER disconnect battery while engine is running (causes 40V+ load-dump spike!). 2. Check all main fuses and scan every ECU for survival. 3. Use DMM & load tester instead.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: 48V Mild Hybrid Belt-Starter Fault (Geely Okavango/Azkarra)
phContext: Geely 48V EMS mild hybrids; 48V battery or BSG inverter fault
symptoms: 48V warning light, Start-Stop & e-boost disabled, runs on 12V/ICE
diagnosticSteps: 1. Scan 48V BSG and BMS modules for cell imbalance or overtemp. 2. Check 48V-to-12V DC-DC converter output. 3. Inspect 48V belt tensioner.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Starter Motor Oil-Soaked — Valve Cover / Rear Main Leak
phContext: Older engines dripping oil directly onto starter below
symptoms: Weak/intermittent cranking, oily sludge inside starter brushes
diagnosticSteps: 1. Fix overhead oil leak (valve cover/distributor/cooler) FIRST! 2. Disassemble and wash starter commutator/brush holder with contact cleaner. 3. Replace worn brushes.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Battery Tray Rusted Through — Vibration Cracking Case
phContext: Coastal/older vehicles; loose battery bouncing on rusted tray
symptoms: Cracked plastic battery corner leaking acid, intermittent power
diagnosticSteps: 1. Remove battery, wire-brush and rust-convert/paint tray. 2. Install proper J-bolt battery hold-down bracket. 3. Replace cracked battery.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: 24V-to-12V Converter Overheating — Overloaded by Accessories
phContext: 24V trucks/buses running 12V fridge + audio + lights on 10A unit
symptoms: 12V accessories cut out after 30 min, converter scorching hot
diagnosticSteps: 1. Sum total 12V accessory amperage and upgrade to 30A–40A continuous DC-DC buck converter. 2. Mount converter in ventilated area away from exhaust heat. 3. Fuse both 24V input and 12V output.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Alternator Brushes Worn Unevenly — Grooved Copper Slip Rings
phContext: 150,000+ km alternators; deep grooves cut into rotor slip rings
symptoms: New brushes fail again within 2 months
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect rotor copper slip rings whenever replacing brushes; deep grooves shred new brushes! 2. Machine/replace copper slip ring assembly and rear bearing. 3. Reassemble.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Fuse Box Main Busbar Loose — Voltage Drop Across Entire Cabin
phContext: Older vehicles with riveted fuse box busbars
symptoms: Headlights, wipers, and blower all dim together when one turns on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure voltage at battery (+) vs. cabin fuse box IG1/B+ rail under full load. 2. Inspect main firewall bulkhead connector for melted/oxidized pins. 3. Repair/bypass.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Parasitic Draw from Stuck Door Handle Capacitive Sensor
phContext: Push-start cars with Smart Entry touch handles after car wash/rain
symptoms: Battery dies overnight, car unlocks/locks by itself
diagnosticSteps: 1. Watch BCM Door Handle Touch Sensor PIDs (one handle stuck ON!). 2. Unplug suspect door handle inside door panel to confirm draw drops <30 mA. 3. Replace handle.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Alternator Whine at Cold Start Only — Battery Recharging Load
phContext: Normal high-ampere charge load right after cranking + cold belt
symptoms: 30-second whine/belt chirp after startup that fades away
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure alternator amperage right after crank (often 60–90A recharging battery!). 2. Check belt tension and battery health (dying battery forces constant max alternator load). 3. Replace belt/battery.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Starter Relay Circuit High — Shorted to 12V
phContext: Aftermarket push-start / remote-start wiring error
symptoms: Starter engages immediately at Key-ON without turning to Start!
diagnosticSteps: 1. Unplug starter relay and trace S-wire back to ignition switch/alarm. 2. Remove shorted aftermarket splice. 3. Verify relay only activates in CRANK position.

domainName: Starting/Charging Edge Cases, Smart Alternators, Stop-Start (ISS) & Mild Hybrid
title: Dead Keyless Fob + Dead Car Battery — Locked Out Completely
phContext: Modern cars with hidden physical keyway under door handle cap
symptoms: Smart key dead and car battery dead, doors won't unlock
diagnosticSteps: 1. Slide mechanical emergency key blade out of smart fob. 2. Pop off plastic keyhole cap at rear of driver door handle (small slot underneath). 3. Unlock door mechanically, pop hood, jump 12V.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: EVAP Emission Control System Malfunction — 'Sagad' Overfill
phContext: Drivers topping off gas past first click; raw liquid fuel flooding canister
symptoms: Fuel smell, hard start after refueling, MIL on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Disconnect charcoal canister vent hose; if liquid gasoline pours out, canister is saturated! 2. Replace saturated charcoal canister and purge valve. 3. Advise stopping at first nozzle click.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: EVAP System Leak Detected (Small Leak) — Dry Filler Neck Hose
phContext: 8+ year old sedans/MPVs; cracked rubber filler-to-tank coupler
symptoms: MIL on, faint fuel odor near left/right rear tire
diagnosticSteps: 1. Smoke-test EVAP system at 1 psi via underhood service port. 2. Inspect rubber coupler hose behind rear wheel liner for dry-rot cracks. 3. Replace hose & clamps.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: EVAP Fuel Tank Pressure (FTP) Sensor Range — Stuck Bias
phContext: Ford, Hyundai, Honda, Toyota; moisture/vapor skewing FTP sensor
symptoms: MIL on, FTP PID stuck at +2.0 kPa or -3.0 kPa with cap off
diagnosticSteps: 1. Remove gas cap! FTP Pressure PID MUST read 0.0 kPa (0.0 inH2O) with cap open! 2. Check 5V, GND, and signal (~2.5V at 0 kPa). 3. Replace FTP sensor.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: EVAP FTP Sensor Circuit Low — Pinched Rear Subframe Wire
phContext: Sedans/crossovers after rear suspension work
symptoms: MIL on, FTP PID reads -5V / max vacuum
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check 5V VREF at FTP sensor plug above fuel tank. 2. Inspect harness pinch point above rear axle. 3. Repair wire.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: EVAP FTP Sensor Circuit High — Open Ground / Rat Bite
phContext: Cars parked outdoors; rodent chewed 3-wire harness above tank
symptoms: MIL on, FTP reads +5V
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check sensor ground continuity to ECM. 2. Drop fuel tank slightly or access via rear seat service hatch to repair chewed wire. 3. Clear DTC.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: EVAP Very Small Leak (0.020 in) — Dirty Gas Cap Seal
phContext: All OBD-II gasoline cars; dust/sand on filler neck lip
symptoms: MIL on intermittently, no driveability symptom
diagnosticSteps: 1. Clean steel/plastic filler neck sealing rim with rag and inspect cap rubber O-ring for hairline cracks. 2. Replace OEM gas cap (avoid cheap non-vented caps!). 3. Clear & monitor.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: EVAP Purge Control Valve Circuit Open — Unplugged / Burned
phContext: Toyota, Hyundai, Suzuki; forgotten plug after airbox/intake service
symptoms: MIL on, zero purge flow
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check 12V IG1 feed at purge solenoid. 2. Measure coil resistance (20–35 ohms). 3. Reconnect or replace solenoid.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: EVAP Purge Control Valve Shorted — Blown Engine Sensor Fuse
phContext: Shorted purge coil blowing shared 10A/15A sensor fuse
symptoms: Multiple sensor codes + P0445, fuse blows immediately at KOEO
diagnosticSteps: 1. Unplug EVAP purge solenoid and verify if fuse holds. 2. Ohm-test solenoid coil (<2 ohms = shorted). 3. Replace purge valve.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: EVAP Vent Control Circuit Open — Corroded Rear Canister Plug
phContext: Crossovers/pickups crossing flooded streets; rear canister under floor
symptoms: MIL on after typhoon season
diagnosticSteps: 1. Locate EVAP canister near rear spare tire/tank. 2. Unplug 2-pin vent solenoid and clean green corrosion. 3. Test 12V & coil resistance.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: EVAP Vent Control Circuit Shorted — Water-Filled Solenoid
phContext: Submerged rear canister vent valve shorting 12V feed
symptoms: MIL on, blown EVAP/ECM fuse
diagnosticSteps: 1. Unplug vent solenoid under rear floor and check for trapped floodwater. 2. Replace waterlogged vent valve and blow out canister filter. 3. Replace fuse.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: EVAP Vent Valve / Solenoid Circuit — Mud-Jammed Plunger
phContext: Pickups/SUVs on muddy provincial roads; solenoid clicks weakly
symptoms: Gas pump shuts off every 2 liters when refueling!
diagnosticSteps: 1. Command vent valve open/closed via scan tool while blowing through vent hose. 2. Remove mud/wasp nest from vent filter box. 3. Replace jammed vent valve.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: EVAP Pressure Sensor Malfunction — Toyota Key-Off Pump
phContext: Toyota Vios/Altis/RAV4 (Leak Detection Pump module on canister)
symptoms: MIL on after car sits 5 hours key-off
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect Toyota EVAP pump module on charcoal canister for floodwater ingress. 2. Command EVAP System Check via Techstream while monitoring pump current & pressure. 3. Replace canister pump module.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: EVAP High Purge Flow During Non-Purge — Stuck Open Purge
phContext: Ford, Hyundai, Kia, GM; purge solenoid leaking manifold vacuum
symptoms: Hard start right after filling gas tank, rough idle
diagnosticSteps: 1. Disconnect purge hose at engine side with engine idling (must have ZERO vacuum!). 2. If vacuum pulls on finger, purge valve is stuck open. 3. Replace purge solenoid.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: EVAP Low Purge Flow — Crushed Plastic Line / Clogged Charcoal
phContext: Cars bottomed out on speed bumps crushing underbody EVAP nylon tube
symptoms: MIL on, P0497
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect plastic EVAP purge line running along floorpan rail for kinks/crushes from jacking or speed bumps! 2. Blow low-pressure air from engine bay to canister to confirm flow. 3. Splice nylon line.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: HO2S Heater Control High (B1S1) — Shorted to 12V
phContext: Aftermarket universal O2 sensor wired incorrectly
symptoms: MIL on immediately, O2 heater driver at risk
diagnosticSteps: 1. Verify OEM O2 wiring pinout (2 heater wires, 1 signal+, 1 signal-). 2. Check heater resistance. 3. Replace with direct-fit OEM-plug sensor.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: HO2S Heater Control Low (B1S2) — Underbody Wire Rub
phContext: Low cars; B1S2 wire rubbing driveshaft or heat shield
symptoms: MIL on, blown heater fuse
diagnosticSteps: 1. Jack car and trace B1S2 pigtail to cabin grommet. 2. Repair rubbed-through insulation. 3. Check fuse.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: O2 Sensor B1S1 High Voltage (>1.0V) — Leaky Injector / Coolant
phContext: Over-fueling cylinder or leaking fuel pressure regulator
symptoms: Black smoke, rich smell, O2 stuck >0.9V
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check fuel pressure and pull FPR vacuum hose to check for raw fuel. 2. Check fuel trims (LTFT < -15%). 3. Fix rich condition before replacing O2.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: O2 Sensor B1S1 Slow Response — Aged Sensor (>100k km)
phContext: High-mileage taxis/commuters; sluggish zirconia ceramic
symptoms: Poor fuel economy, hesitation, MIL on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Graph B1S1 voltage at 2000 RPM (must switch >8 times per 10 sec between 0.1V and 0.8V). 2. If lazy/rounded sine wave, replace upstream O2 sensor.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: O2 Sensor B1S2 Circuit — Cracked Exhaust Gasket
phContext: Cars with loud exhaust tick near catalytic converter
symptoms: B1S2 reads lean/erratic, MIL on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect flange gasket between exhaust manifold/cat and mid-pipe. 2. Check B1S2 wiring under carpet seat grommet. 3. Replace gasket or sensor.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: O2 Sensor B1S2 Low Voltage — Exhaust Leak / Dead Sensor
phContext: Same as P0136; B1S2 stuck <0.15V
symptoms: MIL on, normal driving
diagnosticSteps: 1. Snap-throttle to WOT briefly while watching B1S2 PID (should spike >0.8V on enrichment). 2. If flatlined at 0.05V, check for short to ground or dead sensor. 3. Replace B1S2.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: O2 Sensor B1S2 No Activity — Open Signal / Unplugged
phContext: Cars where catalytic converter was stolen or replaced with test pipe!
symptoms: B1S2 stuck at 0.45V bias, MIL on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Look under car to verify catalytic converter and B1S2 sensor are still physically present! 2. Check 4-pin connector continuity. 3. Replace sensor.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: Rattling Catalytic Converter Substrate — Pothole / Misfire Melt
phContext: High-mileage sedans; broken ceramic honeycomb inside cat shell
symptoms: Loud metallic marble-in-a-can rattle under floor at idle, sudden power loss
diagnosticSteps: 1. Tap catalytic converter shell with rubber mallet when cold (rattle = broken core!). 2. Check exhaust backpressure at B1S1 bung (<15 kPa at 2500 RPM; >20 kPa = clogged!). 3. Replace cat.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: Clogged Catalytic Converter — Engine Won't Rev Past 3000 RPM
phContext: Cars driven with long-term misfire melting cat honeycomb shut
symptoms: Starts fine, idles okay, chokes & stalls under throttle, glowing red cat
diagnosticSteps: 1. Remove upstream O2 sensor (B1S1) temporarily and rev engine: if power instantly returns, exhaust/cat is plugged! 2. Measure exhaust backpressure. 3. Fix misfire cause & replace cat.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: In-Tank Fuel Pump Check Valve Leak — Long Morning Crank
phContext: Older EFI cars; fuel rail drains back to tank overnight
symptoms: Cranks 5–8 sec on first morning start, starts instantly all day
diagnosticSteps: 1. Connect fuel pressure gauge, prime key-on to 350 kPa, turn key off: pressure must hold >200 kPa for 15+ min! 2. Pinch return/supply hose to isolate pump check valve vs. leaky injector. 3. Replace pump.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: Cracked Plastic Fuel Pump Hat — Gas Smell Inside Cabin
phContext: MPVs/sedans with access hatch under 2nd row/rear seat
symptoms: Strong raw gasoline smell inside cabin after filling tank full
diagnosticSteps: 1. Lift rear seat cushion and remove fuel pump service cover. 2. Inspect plastic fuel pump flange top for hairline cracks or pooled fuel around quick-connect! 3. Replace pump flange/O-ring.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: Fuel Pressure Sensor B Range/Performance (Low-Side GDI)
phContext: Modern GDI crossovers (Ford, Hyundai, Kia, Geely); skewed low-side sensor
symptoms: Long cranking, P018B stored
diagnosticSteps: 1. Compare low-side Fuel Pressure PID at KOEO vs. mechanical gauge (400– 550 kPa). 2. Check 5V/GND/signal. 3. Replace low-side pressure sensor.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor A Circuit — Unplugged / Open
phContext: GDI/CRDi engines after manifold removal
symptoms: No start or instant limp mode
diagnosticSteps: 1. Verify 3-pin FRP connector is clicked fully into rail. 2. Check 5V reference and ground. 3. Replace sensor.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: Fuel Pump Module Control Circuit Open — Corroded FPCM
phContext: Ford, Hyundai, Mazda; rear-mounted Fuel Pump Control Module
symptoms: Cranks no start, zero fuel pressure
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check 20A Fuel Pump fuse and FPCM ground on rear chassis. 2. Scope ECM PWM command wire to FPCM. 3. Inspect FPCM housing for water corrosion.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: Fuel Pump Control Module Low — Shorted Pump Motor
phContext: High-mileage in-tank pump drawing >15A and tripping FPCM
symptoms: Stalls hot in traffic, P025C
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure fuel pump current draw with clamp meter (normal 4–7A; >10A = worn commutator!). 2. Check pump resistance (0.8–2.5 ohms). 3. Replace fuel pump.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: Main Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold — Rear Cat
phContext: SUVs with dual-stage cats; aged secondary substrate
symptoms: MIL on, normal performance
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check for exhaust leaks between primary and secondary cat. 2. Verify fuel trims are within +/- 5%. 3. Replace aged catalyst.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: EVAP Purge Control Valve Circuit Low — Shorted Wire
phContext: Pinched EVAP harness under intake manifold
symptoms: MIL on, fuse may blow
diagnosticSteps: 1. Unplug purge valve and check resistance of both pins to ground. 2. Inspect harness near throttle bracket. 3. Repair wire.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: EVAP Purge Control Valve Circuit High — Short to 12V
phContext: Internal ECM driver fault or crossed wire
symptoms: Purge valve stays energized continuously, rough idle
diagnosticSteps: 1. Test purge valve control pin with test light to B+ at KOEO (should be OFF). 2. Trace control wire to ECM for short to 12V. 3. Repair.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: Fuel Level Sensor A Range/Performance — Dual-Saddle Tank
phContext: AWD SUVs/pickups with split saddle fuel tank (2 senders!)
symptoms: Fuel gauge jumps erratically or sticks at 1/2 tank
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read BOTH Main and Sub Fuel Level PIDs on scan tool! 2. Inspect jet-pump transfer siphon hose inside tank (if disconnected, one side stays full). 3. Clean/replace faulty sender.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit Low — Shorted Float Arm
phContext: Fuel sender wire pinched during fuel filter service
symptoms: Fuel gauge drops to Empty with warning light
diagnosticSteps: 1. Unplug fuel pump module under rear seat; check if gauge swings to Full (or reads open). 2. Inspect sender resistor card and ground. 3. Replace sender.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit High — Open Wiper / Rat Bite
phContext: Chewed wire on top of fuel tank or worn silver-palladium wiper
symptoms: Fuel gauge stuck Full or Empty depending on OEM logic
diagnosticSteps: 1. Jump sender signal pin to sensor ground briefly with 100-ohm resistor; gauge should move! 2. If gauge moves, fault is in-tank sender/ground. 3. Replace sender.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: Unable to Bleed Up Fuel Tank Vacuum (Ford) — Stuck Purge
phContext: Ford EcoSport/Fiesta/Ranger/E xplorer; tank imploding noise
symptoms: Loud 'pop/thump' from under car, gas tank sucks inward, stalls after refuel
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check EVAP purge valve (stuck open pulls full manifold vacuum on gas tank!). 2. Check canister vent valve for mud/spiderweb blockage! 3. Replace stuck purge/vent valve.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: Post-Catalyst Fuel Trim Too Rich — Fouled B1S2 / Injector
phContext: GDI/EFI cars running rich or burning oil
symptoms: MIL on, B1S2 voltage stuck >0.8V
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check B1S1 trims and injector leak-down first. 2. Swap/inspect B1S2 for oil fouling. 3. Fix upstream rich source.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: O2 Sensor Signal Stuck Rich (B1S1) — High Fuel Pressure
phContext: Failed mechanical fuel pressure regulator or leaky injector
symptoms: Black smoke, fouled plugs, LTFT -20%
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check fuel rail pressure (too high = stuck FPR or pinched return line!). 2. Pull vacuum hose off FPR to check for fuel. 3. Replace FPR/injector.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: O2/AF Sensor Reference Voltage Open (B1S1) — Wideband
phContext: Toyota/Honda wideband A/F sensor; broken reference wire
symptoms: MIL on, A/F reading frozen
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect 4/6-pin A/F connector for pushed-out pin. 2. Check continuity to ECM. 3. Replace wideband sensor.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: O2/AF Sensor Negative Current Control Open (B1S1)
phContext: Wideband A/F sensor wire damage from road debris
symptoms: MIL on, fuel trim disabled
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect underbody harness near bellhousing. 2. Verify pin tension at ECM and sensor plug. 3. Replace sensor if harness intact.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: Fuel Tank Rust / Sediment Clogging Pump Sock Every Month
phContext: Older 15+ year metal-tank vehicles; water rusting tank inside
symptoms: Car loses power at high RPM, new fuel filter turns brown in weeks
diagnosticSteps: 1. Pull fuel pump assembly and shine flashlight (never open flame!) into tank to check for flaking rust. 2. Drop tank for chemical cleaning/epoxy lining or replace tank. 3. Replace sock.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: Aftermarket O2 Spacer / Defouler Causing P0139 Slow Response
phContext: Modified cars with cat-delete + mechanical spark-plug defouler
symptoms: MIL returns with P0139/P0140 even though P0420 went away
diagnosticSteps: 1. Remove mechanical spacer blocking exhaust flow to B1S2 sensor. 2. Restore proper OEM catalytic converter for LTO compliance and proper closed-loop trim.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: Refueling Nozzle Keeps Clicking Off — Clogged Canister Vent
phContext: Dusty provincial cars; mud/insects plugging fresh-air vent line
symptoms: Takes 10 minutes to pump P500 of gas, splash-back
diagnosticSteps: 1. Disconnect fresh-air vent hose from charcoal canister (usually routed up to fuel filler pocket or rear frame). 2. Blow out spider/wasp mud nest! 3. Check rollover valve in tank.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: EVAP System High Pressure / Purge Line Blocked
phContext: Modern Euro-5/6 cars with dual-path turbo EVAP venturi
symptoms: MIL on, normal driving
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect EVAP check-valve tee between intake manifold and turbo inlet. 2. Check for pinched hose. 3. Test purge solenoid.

domainName: Fuel Tank, EVAP Leaks, Charcoal Canister & Exhaust Aftertreatment
title: Exhaust Muffler / Resonator Waterlogged — Short-Trip Corrosion
phContext: City cars driven <3 km per trip; acidic condensation rusting muffler
symptoms: Gurgling exhaust sound, rusted pinhole drips under rear bumper
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect muffler bottom seam for rust pinholes. 2. Advise occasional 20-min highway drives to boil off acidic exhaust water. 3. Replace rusted muffler.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: Bench ECU Fails to Power Up / Zero Current Draw (<10 mA)
phContext: Denso / Bosch / Continental ECU on bench 16-pin harness
symptoms: No CAN activity, scan tool cannot connect on bench
diagnosticSteps: 1. Verify KL30 (Battery +), KL15 (Ignition +), and GND pins against OEM pinout (never guess!). 2. Check Main Relay feedback pin (many Toyota/Mitsubishi ECUs need MREL bridged to 12V to wake CPU!). 3. Check reverse-polarity protection diode on PCB.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: Internal 5V Regulator IC Dropout on Bench — Dead TLE4267/TLE6368
phContext: Bosch ME7.5, Ford SID208, Denso ECUs; shorted external 5V sensor cooked IC
symptoms: VREF_5V reads 0V or 1.8V on bench with zero sensors attached, regulator IC scorching hot
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure VREF_5V on bench with all external load disconnected. 2. Feel 5V power management IC (e.g., Bosch 30344 / Infineon TLE) for extreme heat. 3. Check 5V rail resistance to GND; replace shorted decoupling cap or 5V regulator IC.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: Ignition Coil Driver IGBT Shorted Closed — Melts External Coil
phContext: Bosch ME7.5 / Hyundai / Nissan ECUs with internal coil drivers
symptoms: Cylinder #1 coil overheats & blows fuse immediately at Key-ON!
diagnosticSteps: 1. On bench, check continuity from IGT1 pin to ECU GND (shorted IGBT stays permanently grounded!). 2. Desolder shorted TO-252/DPAK IGBT (e.g., VB325SP / ISL9V3040) and check gate resistor (100–330 Ω). 3. Scope 5V gate trigger before soldering new IGBT.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: Injector Low-Side Driver MOSFET Open/Shorted — Dead Cylinder
phContext: Denso / Mitsubishi E6T / Bosch ECUs after shorted injector or water
symptoms: Cylinder #1 injector stays locked ON (floods cylinder) or never pulses
diagnosticSteps: 1. Scope injector driver pin on bench while injecting simulated CKP 60-2 signal. 2. Measure drain-to-source on PCB MOSFET array / smart driver IC (e.g., TLE6220 / L9132). 3. Replace failed driver IC.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: CAN Transceiver IC (TJA1040 / TJA1050) Fried by 12V Short
phContext: Any CAN ECU after jump-start surge or OBD splitter shorting Pin 6/14 to 12V
symptoms: ECU powers up (normal 150–250 mA draw) but zero CAN comm & 120 Ω missing/shorted
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure resistance across ECU CAN-H/CAN-L pins on bench (must be ~120 Ω if terminating ECU, or high-Z if non-terminating). 2. Scope TXD/RXD pins on 8-pin SOIC CAN transceiver! 3. Replace TJA1040/TJA1050 + split-cap/choke.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: Toyota / Denso ECU No-Start After Water — Corroded PCB Via
phContext: Toyota Vios/Innova/Hilux Denso ECU exposed to windshield/firewall leak
symptoms: Intermittent no-spark or no-fuel-pump relay trigger
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect ECU PCB under microscope around perimeter connector pins and conformal coating bubbles. 2. Test continuity across discolored copper vias from top layer to bottom layer. 3. Ultrasonic clean PCB in IPA and jumper dead vias with 0.1mm enamel wire.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: ECU Internal Checksum / Flash Corruption — Interrupted OBD Flash
phContext: Bosch/Continental/Denso ECUs after failed KTAG/OBD tuning or low voltage
symptoms: Car cranks no start, MIL off, P0601 permanent, OBD write fails
diagnosticSteps: 1. Connect ECU in Boot Mode / BDM / JTAG on bench (requires boot pin to GND/3.3V per datasheet). 2. Read full Flash + EEPROM backup FIRST! 3. Flash verified OEM stock bin and recalculate checksums.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: Internal ROM/EEPROM Error — Corrupted Immobilizer / VIN Block
phContext: Mitsubishi, Hyundai, Toyota ECUs after dead-battery cranking
symptoms: Cranks no start, P0605/P1600 active, immobilizer won't pair
diagnosticSteps: 1. Desolder or clip-read 8-pin SOIC EEPROM (e.g., 93C56 / 93C86 / 95080 / 24C02) with programmer. 2. Inspect hex dump for FF-wiped blocks or corrupted ISN/VIN. 3. Write virgin/immo-matched dump.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: Electronic Throttle H-Bridge Driver IC Fault (TLE6209 / L9958)
phContext: Gasoline ECUs (Bosch ME7.5, Mitsubishi, Toyota) with dead ETC motor drive
symptoms: Throttle butterfly doesn't sweep at KOEO, limp mode
diagnosticSteps: 1. On bench, command throttle sweep or check H-bridge IC 12V VBAT pin (often fed by separate Actuator fuse/pin!). 2. Scope OUT1/OUT2 PWM waveforms. 3. Replace blown H-bridge IC.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: Ford SID208 / Piezo Diesel ECU High-Voltage Boost Converter Dead
phContext: Ford Ranger/Everest 2.2/3.2 SID208; moisture or shorted piezo injector
symptoms: All 4 injectors dead, zero 140V–180V boost voltage on scope
diagnosticSteps: 1. WARNING: High voltage (150V+) on SID208 capacitor! Discharge safely before probing. 2. Check boost inductor, Schottky diode, and boost MOSFET on PCB. 3. Replace shorted components and test injector insulation before re-installing!

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: Bench CKP 60-2 RPM Simulation Fails to Wake ECU — Pull-Up/Bias
phContext: Technician testing VR vs. Hall ECU on bench simulator
symptoms: ECU powers on, draws 200 mA, but RPM stays 0 on scan tool
diagnosticSteps: 1. Verify whether ECU expects Inductive VR (differential +/- AC sine/zero-crossing) vs. Hall-effect (0– 5V/12V square wave with pull-up)! 2. Add DC-blocking cap or 1kΩ pull-up on bench emulator. 3. Match exact CKP+CMP tooth pattern.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: Electrolytic Capacitor Leak Eating PCB Traces (90s–2000s ECUs)
phContext: Older Mitsubishi (E6T/MD), Nissan, Toyota ECUs; aged caps leaking acid
symptoms: Fishy odor inside ECU, erratic fuel pump/idle, random stalls
diagnosticSteps: 1. Open ECU lid and inspect cylindrical electrolytic caps for crust/wetness at base! 2. Desolder leaked caps, neutralize alkaline electrolyte, and repair eaten copper traces. 3. Install 105°C low-ESR Nichicon/Panasonic caps.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: ECU Main Relay Driver Pin Shorted/Open — Burned Transistor
phContext: Toyota/Honda/Mitsubishi ECUs; external relay shorted coil cooked driver
symptoms: Main relay never clicks ON when key turns ON (must jumper relay to start)
diagnosticSteps: 1. Trace MREL / IGSW pin on PCB back to low-side NPN/MOSFET driver. 2. Measure transistor junction with diode mode. 3. Replace burned driver transistor & faulty external relay.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: Bench Scan Tool Fails K-Line Init — Wrong Baud / Missing Pull-Up
phContext: Older KWP2000 / ISO 9141 ECUs on bench harness
symptoms: Scan tool says 'ECU Not Responding' on Pin 7
diagnosticSteps: 1. Verify K-Line (Pin 7) has 510 Ω–1 kΩ pull-up to 12V (inside ECU or VCI). 2. Check if ECU requires L-Line (Pin 15) 5-baud wakeup! 3. Scope Pin 7 for 0– 12V init pulse.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: Radiator Fan Relay Driver IC Dead — Continuous Fan Run
phContext: ECUs where fan relay ground driver shorted internally to GND
symptoms: Cooling fan runs the instant key turns ON even at 25°C cold
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check ECT PID (if 25°C and A/C off, ECM shouldn't command fan!). 2. Trace FAN1 pin on PCB to multi-channel low-side driver IC. 3. Replace driver IC.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: A/C Clutch Relay Driver Open — Cold Aircon Dead
phContext: Toyota/Mitsubishi/Hyundai ECUs; A/C clutch relay coil shorted driver
symptoms: A/C button works, pressure OK, ECM requests A/C but clutch relay stays off
diagnosticSteps: 1. Monitor 'A/C Request' vs. 'A/C Clutch Relay' PIDs. 2. Ground relay control pin momentarily at ECM plug (if clutch engages, ECM driver is open!). 3. Repair ECM driver.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: Crystal Oscillator (Quartz) Cracked — Dropped ECU
phContext: ECU dropped on workshop concrete floor
symptoms: ECU draws fixed 30 mA, CPU completely dead, zero CAN/K-Line
diagnosticSteps: 1. Probe MCU crystal oscillator pins (4–20 MHz) with 10x oscilloscope probe (must show clean sine wave). 2. Inspect SMD quartz crystal for cracked solder pads. 3. Replace crystal.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: O2 Heater Low-Side Driver Burned — Unfused Heater Short
phContext: ECUs after underbody O2 harness melted onto exhaust pipe
symptoms: New O2 sensor still throws P0135/P0141 immediately
diagnosticSteps: 1. Test 12V at O2 heater pin, then scope ECM ground-control pin (stays at 12V, never pulls to 0V). 2. Trace pin on PCB to quad-driver IC. 3. Replace driver IC.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: Bench Power Supply Trips Current Limit (>3A) — Shorted TVS Diode
phContext: ECU after jump-start polarity reversal or 24V jump on 12V car!
symptoms: ECU blows main EFI fuse immediately when plugged in
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check large SMBJ/SMBJ18A TVS protection diode across KL30/KL15 input to GND (shorts dead to protect CPU!). 2. Desolder shorted TVS diode; if short clears, test ECU! 3. Solder new 18V/24V TVS diode.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: Toyota 1KD/2KD EDU High-Voltage DC-DC Failure — No Injector Fire
phContext: Separate Denso EDU box on Hilux/Fortuner/HiAce; vibration solder crack
symptoms: Engine cranks, rail pressure builds 35 MPa, zero injector pulse, P0200
diagnosticSteps: 1. Open EDU sealed lid carefully and inspect heavy transformer/inductor legs and 100V caps for ring cracks in solder! 2. Reflow heavy leads with leaded/silver solder. 3. Bench-test boost output.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: BGA / QFP MCU Cold Solder Joint — Works Only When Pressed/Heated
phContext: Bosch/Continental/Motorol a MPC5xx/TC17xx ECUs in engine bay heat
symptoms: Car stalls when engine bay hits 80°C, restarts if ECU cooled with ice/spray
diagnosticSteps: 1. On bench, apply gentle localized hot-air (60–80°C) or freeze spray over MCU/flash while monitoring CAN/current. 2. Reflow QFP pins with flux or reball BGA professionally. 3. Verify thermal stability.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: MIL / Check Engine Lamp Driver Dead — Lamp Never Lights at KOEO
phContext: Older ECUs; burned bulb or ECM lamp driver transistor
symptoms: Engine runs fine or no-start, Check Engine Light dead at Key-ON
diagnosticSteps: 1. Verify cluster bulb/LED first. 2. Trace MIL pin on PCB to small NPN transistor/driver. 3. Replace transistor.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: Nissan Hitachi / MEC ECU Idle Air Control (IACV) STA509A Burned
phContext: Older Nissan Sentra/X-Trail/Urvan; coolant leak into IACV shorts ECU
symptoms: Idle stuck at 2000 RPM or stalls; burnt chip smell inside ECU
diagnosticSteps: 1. CRITICAL: Replace leaking coolant-heated IACV on throttle body FIRST! 2. Open Nissan ECU and inspect 10-pin SIP IC (STA509A) — usually visibly cracked/charred! 3. Replace STA509A.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: Mitsubishi E6T / Lancer / Adventure ECU — Corrupted Flash/Immo
phContext: Mitsubishi ECUs; battery drain during cranking corrupting EEPROM
symptoms: Cranks fine, zero spark/injector, immobilizer active
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read ECU flash via Tactrix/OpenPort/bench J2534. 2. Verify immobilizer sync bytes or pair key via MUT-III. 3. Check 5V sensor rails.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: CAN Common-Mode Choke Open — Knocked Off PCB / Burned
phContext: ECUs hit by static/ESD or physical pry during cover removal
symptoms: 120-ohm resistor checks OK inside ECU, yet zero CAN reaches pins
diagnosticSteps: 1. Trace CAN-H/L connector pins to tiny 4-pin SMD common-mode choke next to transceiver! 2. Test continuity across both choke coils (must be <1 ohm). 3. Replace broken choke.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: Bench Harness Missing 120-Ohm Terminating Resistor — No Comm
phContext: Technician testing non-terminating ECU (like TCM/ABS/BCM) alone on bench
symptoms: Scan tool fails to talk to isolated module on bench
diagnosticSteps: 1. Remember: High-Speed CAN requires TWO 120-ohm resistors (60 ohms total) on the bus! 2. Flip 120-ohm (or 60-ohm) termination switch ON on your bench harness! 3. Retry scan.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: USB-to-VCI (J2534 / V200) Driver Dropouts — Poor USB OTG Cable
phContext: Technician flashing/scanning via Android USB OTG or laptop
symptoms: VCI disconnects mid-scan or fails J2534 voltage check
diagnosticSteps: 1. Use short, shielded high-data USB cable (cheap charging cables drop packets!). 2. Check OTG power supply and Pin 16 vehicle voltage (>12.5V stable!). 3. Verify VCI firmware match.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: Internal Control Module RAM Error — Static / Faulty SRAM
phContext: Older/damaged ECUs; failed external/internal RAM self-test
symptoms: MIL on, limp mode, P0604 returns immediately on clear
diagnosticSteps: 1. Verify clean 5V/3.3V core supply rails on PCB (check ripple with scope). 2. Replace faulty ECU if internal MCU RAM failed.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: Sensor Ground (SGND) Trace Burned Open Inside ECU
phContext: Mechanic accidentally touched 12V test light to 5V sensor ground wire!
symptoms: MAP, ECT, IAT, TPS all read maxed out simultaneously!
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure continuity between ECU Sensor Ground (SGND) pin and main Power Ground (PGND) pin on bench (often connected via a 0-ohm jumper or thin fuse trace!). 2. Repair burned SGND PCB trace.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: 3.3V / 1.8V Core LDO Regulator Dead — Modern TriCore/Renesas ECU
phContext: Newer Tricore TC1797 / TC275 / Renesas ECUs; 150 mA drops to 5 mA
symptoms: ECU dead, 5V VREF may be off or on, MCU stays cold
diagnosticSteps: 1. Probe 3.3V and 1.25V/1.8V MCU core test pads on PCB. 2. Check for shorted ceramic bypass cap near MCU. 3. Replace PMIC/LDO.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: Alternator PWM/LIN Driver Damaged Inside ECU
phContext: Ford/Hyundai/Mazda ECUs after alternator regulator short
symptoms: Battery light stays on, charging fixed at 13.5V fallback
diagnosticSteps: 1. Scope LIN/PWM wire at ECU pin disconnected from alternator (must output clean 0–12V command). 2. Trace pin to LIN transceiver (e.g., TJA1020/1021) or pull-up resistor on PCB. 3. Replace LIN IC.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: Conformal Coating / Silicone Gel Blocking Probe Contact
phContext: Waterproofed ECUs (Bosch/Denso/Delphi) with thick silicone gel
symptoms: False 'open circuit' readings when probing PCB test pads
diagnosticSteps: 1. Use sharp needle-tip multimeter probes or gently scrape clear conformal coating off test pads with fiberglass pen. 2. Reseal repaired area with conformal coating spray.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: Control Module Performance — Sub-CPU Watchdog Reset Loop
phContext: Toyota/Denso dual-CPU ECUs; main CPU & sub-CPU out of sync
symptoms: Throttle cuts out randomly, P0607
diagnosticSteps: 1. Verify 5V supply stability and clock crystal. 2. Inspect SPI/communication traces between Main MCU and Watchdog Sub-CPU. 3. Replace ECU if watchdog fails.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: EEPROM Pin 8 VCC Missing — Cold Solder After Re-Work
phContext: ECU previously opened for immo-off / odometer / crash reset
symptoms: Car no-start after shop work, checksum/immo fault
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect 8-pin SOIC EEPROM under microscope for lifted pads, solder bridges, or upside-down Pin 1 orientation! 2. Verify 5V/3.3V on Pin 8. 3. Resolder cleanly.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: Bench Fuel Injector / Coil Test Burns Out Without Current Limit
phContext: Bench testing GDI/piezo or low-ohm diesel injector with raw 12V
symptoms: Injector coil overheats in 2 seconds!
diagnosticSteps: 1. NEVER hold constant 12V DC on a <3 ohm GDI or diesel injector! 2. Use current-limited bench driver (peak-and-hold PWM) or 0–30V/10A supply with current limit set. 3. Verify coil resistance first.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
title: VVT / OCV Driver Stuck ON — Cam Over-Advanced at Idle
phContext: Toyota/Honda ECUs; shorted low-side OCV MOSFET
symptoms: Engine stalls at idle, runs okay at 3000 RPM, P0011
diagnosticSteps: 1. Unplug OCV; if idle smooths out, OCV is being held open! 2. Test OCV control wire at KOEO (must NOT be grounded!). 3. Replace shorted driver on PCB.

domainName: Bench ECU Testing, PCB Component & Driver IC Faults (AutoElectric Lab PRO)
